notes: Evals 1, 2 and 4 are self-contained: their fixtures live in evals/fixtures/ inside this skill (4 reuses 1's fixtures to test report-language selection). Substitute the absolute path of the skill directory for <SKILL_DIR> when running them. Eval 3 is a template that needs a target repo supplied at run time — any codebase with a stateful lifecycle works; it must NOT hardcode a specific project. Runs write a report under systemic-out/; because the fixtures are a fixture directory and not the grader's own project, the skill should place it under the working directory rather than inside evals/fixtures/. Clean it between runs so a stale file is not mistaken for a fresh one.

evals.name: seeded-defects-code
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the orders module at <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/orders/ (README.md, models.py, operations.py, webhook.py). I want to find inconsistencies in its states and operations before it reaches production.
evals.expected_output: A report following the skill's exact structure that models the orders system (elements, operators, declared vs built machine) and detects the 9 seeded flaws with file:line evidence, honesty labels and severities, plus a missing-piece synthesis.
assertions: Detects the closure violation: refund() writes status 'refund_pending' which is not in the STATUS set (models.py vs operations.py)
Detects the illegal representable state: mark_paid() sets paid_at/status without any guard on current status (a draft order can become paid)
Detects the declared-vs-built contradiction: cancel() has no guard while the README forbids canceling a shipped order
Detects the ambiguous operator: apply_discount() switches semantics on value<=1 (fraction vs absolute) while the README says percentage 0-100
Detects the broken symmetry: hold() exists but no release/resume operation exists anywhere in the module
Detects the unreachable state: in_review is declared (README + STATUS) but no operation ever produces it
Detects the idempotency flaw: handle_payment_webhook() has no dedup by event_id although the README warns the provider retries/duplicates
Detects the double source of truth: Order.total stored while calc_total() exists, and add_item() does not update total
Detects the partial-failure risk in ship(): inventory reserved, courier.notify may raise, status not yet written, no transaction/compensation
Report includes a mermaid state diagram
Every finding carries an honesty label (INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY)
Every finding carries a severity (critical/high/medium/low)
Findings cite file:line (or file+function) evidence
Report includes a missing-piece/root-cause synthesis (e.g. a single guarded transition operator would prevent several findings at once)
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
No artifact is published, no HTML is rendered and no server/localhost preview is started to display the report

evals.name: design-doc-only
evals.prompt: Here is a design document for an equipment rental feature: <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/rental-doc/DESIGN.md. Without looking at any code, is the described design systemically consistent? What ambiguities or holes does the document have?
evals.expected_output: A document-only systemic analysis: models the rental lifecycle as a conceptual machine (mermaid), and surfaces the seeded contradictions, ambiguities and holes citing only sections/lines of the document, with honesty labels and severities.
assertions: Models the rental lifecycle as a conceptual state machine derived from the document
Detects the declared-vs-declared contradiction: 'overdue rentals can never be extended' vs the extend() example of a customer two days late extending
Detects the idempotency/double-refund risk: locker return events may fire multiple times while each return event triggers the deposit refund
Detects that 'suspended' (business rule 3) is used but absent from the declared state list — an unrepresentable state
Detects the double source of truth: invoice total stored at approval time vs price defined as daily_rate × days actually rented (extension/late return drift)
Flags the deposit-refund condition as AMBIGUITY: 'good condition' undefined (who decides, when, no timeline)
Detects the hole for lost items: handled 'outside the system' with no transition, leaving the rental machine stuck in active/overdue
Evidence cites only sections/lines of the document (no code paths)
Report includes a mermaid state diagram
Every finding carries an honesty label (INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY)
Every finding carries a severity (critical/high/medium/low)
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
No artifact is published, no HTML is rendered and no server/localhost preview is started to display the report

evals.name: real-repo-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the <LIFECYCLE> state machine in <TARGET_REPO_PATHS>. Is the lifecycle consistent?
evals.expected_output: Models the target lifecycle from the real code: its actual states (no invented ones), operators mapped to transitions, mermaid diagram of the built machine, findings with file:line evidence, honesty labels and severities, and a limits/not-verified section.
assertions: Identifies the real states of the target lifecycle from the code and does not invent states that do not exist
Maps the key operators to transitions (which operation executes each transition)
Report includes a mermaid state diagram of the built machine
Report includes an explicit system model (elements and operators listed, not just prose)
Findings cite file:line evidence
Every finding carries an honesty label (INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY) and a severity
Report includes a limits/not-verified section stating which checks did not apply
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
No artifact is published, no HTML is rendered and no server/localhost preview is started to display the report

evals.name: explicit-report-language
evals.prompt: Haz un análisis sistémico del módulo de órdenes en <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/orders/, pero escribe el reporte en inglés.
evals.expected_output: The same systemic report as eval 1, written entirely in English because the user asked for it explicitly, even though the request itself is in Spanish — with the honesty labels and severities left as fixed keywords.
assertions: The report's section headers and prose are in English, following the explicit request rather than the language of the prompt
Honesty labels stay as the fixed keywords INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY (not translated)
Severities stay as the fixed keywords critical/high/medium/low (not translated)
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
Detects at least the closure violation and the missing-guard findings from eval 1 (language choice does not degrade the analysis)
